subject: SkyBridge pilot — fleet projection & token-tail probe
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@skybridge.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+cloud@skybridge.ai
Date: Thu, 09 May 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: SkyBridge pilot — kickoff data for fleet projection

Hey Logan,

Thanks for taking this — excited to get Redwood involved for our pilot. High level: we want a dedicated cluster to serve a customer-facing multimodal assistant (text + small image inputs) with strict tail latency goals for premium users. A few details up front so you can start a sizing sketch: 

- Typical prompt / request mix: 70% short Q&A (prompt ~25–80 tokens), 25% conversational threads (prompt ~120–250 tokens, responses 200–600 tokens), 5% similarity/embedding calls (single 768-d vector per call).
- Expected concurrency: baseline 60 concurrent sessions during business hours, with bursts up to ~450 concurrent active sessions during product launches.
- Peak QPS (token generation requests): sustained 180 qps with short bursts to 750 qps for 90–180s.
- Latency target: p95 < 120ms for short Q&A paths; p99 < 600ms for long generative threads (we accept streaming for long responses).
- Session behavior: approx 1.7 messages per session on average, top 3% of sessions produce long chains (6+ messages).
- Models we expect to run: Llama-2/Redwood-optimized 13B variants (quantized) for most traffic; we may route some high-quality paid traffic to an unquantized 13B-opt.

I've attached a short token histogram (token_histogram_q1.csv) and a tiny sample of telemetry. Can you send over your preflight template with the fields we should populate? Also please call out what you need around KV cache persistence and prefix-caching for our conversational paths.

Cheers,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform
SkyBridge AI

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 May 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SkyBridge pilot — fleet projection & token-tail probe

Elena — thanks for the context and the histogram, very helpful. Sending our preflight template and a short checklist so we can converge quickly. Attached: SB-preflight-template.xlsx (spreadsheet) and a 1‑page note with what we typically assume for dedicated pilots.

Highlights / items we need you to fill in on the spreadsheet:
- Traffic breakdown by route (api/chat, api/complete, embedding) — percent and expected QPS windows (sustained / peak bursts).
- Prompt/response token percentiles you can provide (p50, p90, p99) for each route.
- Session stickiness (how long does a user keep an open session / how often do they re-use session id).
- Concurrency semantics: are multiple requests multiplexed over a session, or single-threaded per session?
- Expected % of streaming responses vs full-response generation.
- Any long-running background tasks (e.g., async re-ranking, batch embeddings) that would hit the same fleet.

Technical notes:
- KV cache sizing: for conversation flows where we expect 6–10 turns, we recommend allocating KV capacity per active session (and we can share a default bytes-per-token estimate in the template). If you want prefix-caching (e.g., static system prompts / user profile prefixes), that helps reduce compute on long threads.
- Models: quantized 13B gives very favorable token economics; we will show tradeoffs for routing a small % to unquantized 13B-opt for high-quality paid users during our estimate.

Proposed next step: please populate the attached sheet and return by Mon 13 May. If you prefer, share a 20–30s sample of live telemetry (slimmed down) and Vivek will run a quick throughput sim and give a ballpark GPU count.

Logan Wright
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Logan / team — attached is a filled version of your template (see SB-preflight-template.xlsx) and a sanitized telemetry sample (sb_telemetry_sample.jsonl). Key answers inline below: 

- Route split (sustained): api/chat 62%, api/complete 33%, embedding 5%. Peak burst splits similar.
- Token percentiles (api/chat): prompt p50=95, p90=260, p99=540; response p50=160, p90=420, p99=1180. For api/complete prompt p50=12, p90=48, p99=200; response p50=32, p90=160, p99=600.
- Concurrency: sessions are single-threaded per user (we do not multiplex), but our mobile client will open up to 3 concurrent connections per user during retries.
- Streaming: ~28% of chat responses use streaming.
- Burst profile: most bursts align with marketing emails and product drops — windows of 60–180s; the telemetry sample shows a 10x spike in sessions.
- KV usage: typical conversation history kept for 8 turns; we also append a user profile (~250 tokens) as a prefix for paid users.

Attaching sample files. Let us know what else you need.

Elena

Elena — this is great, thanks for the filled sheet and the telemetry sample. Quick summary of next steps from our side and what to expect: 

1) Vivek will run the sample through a throughput & tail-sim in the next 48 hours. Expect a back-of-envelope of GPU count and a recommended mix (e.g., 8x A10G-like nodes in quantized 13B pool + 1x high-fidelity 13B-opt node for paid traffic).
2) We'll call out KV cache sizing assumptions and an option to offload long prefixes to Redis to reduce per-GPU memory overhead — initial recommendation: keep 80MB/session-equivalent headroom for top 5% sessions; we will quantify after the sim.
3) Scheduling: propose a 30-minute sync Tue 14 May 10:00 AM PT to walk through the sim and capture constraints (SLA, burst windows, expected cutover date). Calendar invite to follow.
4) Deliverable after sync: provisional capacity workbook (GPU SKU mix, throughput by route, expected costs) and a short ops playbook for rolling canary traffic.

If anything changes on your side (e.g., adding a new embedding-heavy feature), loop us in so we can re-run. Otherwise we’ll aim to circulate the estimate by Wed 15 May.

Thanks — Logan
